articles.title: Save 42% Off the PS Portal, the Only Way You'll Be Able to Play Grand Theft Auto 6 on a Handheld
articles.summary: Forget the price hike.GTA 6 will only be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox, to start out.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is out in November, but only for two platforms: PlayStation 5 and Xbox. That means you won't be able to play it on a handheld gaming PC or Switch 2 portable console for quite a while. If you do want to play Grand Theft Auto on a mobile type device from the comfort of your bed or couch away from the TV, the only easy way will be by using a PlayStation Portal connected to your PS5 console Fortunately, there's a way to get a massive discount on one today.

Xbox gamers can do the same with Xbox Ally using Remote Play, but the cost to own both devices is greater.

PlayStation Portal (Used: Very Good) for $147

Amazon Resale just dropped the price of the "Used: Very Good" PS Portal to $146.99 after a 30% off coupon that's automatically applied during checkout. This is an excellent deal considering the fact that Sony raised the retail price of the PS Portal from $200 to $250 just a few months ago . Amazon Resale is Amazon's official outlet for used items. Amazon states that this "Very Good" item "looks and functions as if it were new. Item may not come in original packaging." You still get the 30-day Amazon return policy so it's a much safer option than buying a used controller off Facebook Marketplace.

The PS Portal, Sony's handheld gaming accessory for the PS5 console , looks very much like an extended split-pad DualSense controller with an 8-inch 1080p LCD screen in the middle of it. It turns your PS5 into a gaming handheld by letting you stream games from your console at up to 60fps. The controller mirrors the same features found on the DualSense, including haptic feedback, adaptive triggers, and a touchscreen interface that replaces the Dualsense's touchpad. The Portal can stream your games even when you're outside of your home, with the caveat that you have access to very stable, very fast internet connection. Keep in mind that the PS Portal is not a standalone device. This is strictly a remote player for the PlayStation 5, so you will need a PS5 to use it.

You no longer need a PS5 to play games on the PS Portal . Now, rather than being limited to simply streaming games from a $500 console to a $200 handheld, Sony has introduced a feature that lets owners stream games directly from its PlayStation Now cloud streaming service. No PS5 required. Portal owners can either connect the Portal to their PS5 or directly to Sony’s cloud servers (with some new quality of life beta updates that launched in April ). Choose the latter and suddenly you have access to a library of more than 120 games, including Ghost of Tsushima, Resident Evil 3 Remake, The Last of Us Part 1 Remastered, and Marvel’s Spider-Man: Miles Morales. It’s worth noting you must be a subscriber to the highest tier of PlayStation Plus , but $18 a month is much more attractive than paying for every new game.

It should be said that the PlayStation Portal isn’t the only way to stream your PS5 games over Wi-Fi within your home. You can mimic its functionality by downloading the PS Remote Play app on a mobile device, including other gaming handhelds like the Steam Deck. That said, it's more complicated to set up and you'll lose out on some of the DualSense's features.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.title: 12 Game, Movie, and TV Show Trailers You Might Have Missed This Week
articles.summary: This week's trailer bounty included the extended look at Grand Theft Auto 6, tons of footage from gamescom, a first look at the new Pokémon stop-motion series coming to Disney+, a new Ali G movie, and lots more.
articles.body:
It’s been a huge week for trailers, specifically for games (though the entertainment front hardly took the week off). Of course, the big headline from this week is GTA 6. (Did your Netflix break when you tried to log on to watch the Extended Look right when it dropped?) But gamescom has also been busy shelling out one trailer after another since Tuesday’s Opening Night Live . What’s included here is merely a tiny smattering of the biggest hits; you can peruse all of them — there are currently 187 — at your leisure on IGN’s YouTube channel .

Here are the trailers you should watch from this week (and here’s what you missed last week ).

In the trailer event to end all trailer events, Rockstar finally dropped a long 27-minute look at the most anticipated game of the decade after enduring a series of brutal leaks (that seems like it might also have been a crypto scheme ). What else is there to say that my esteemed colleagues have not already ? Obviously, it looks insane.

GTA 6 is coming out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

There’s tons of new footage from Fable that you can check out from gamescom — plus, read our preview — but I was particularly drawn to these 18 minutes of quest gameplay that takes the Hero through the massive and gorgeous Bowerstone (130 homes and 30 businesses and you can go in all of them??? ), highlights some character interactions (I also would have thrown the beer at Humphry), and shows off a tiny bit of combat (I scrubbed back on shooting that one thug in the knee with an arrow like three times, very good).

Fable releases on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC on February 23, 2027.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered + Songs of the Past DLC

The Witcher 3 got a twofer out of gamescom 2026: a remaster trailer (which will be free for players who already own the game ) and the Songs of the Past DLC. Any excuse to hang out with Geralt another time is cool in my book. The Remaster, of course, looks super slick, but Songs of the Past especially has me intrigued with the freakiness of Letten.

The Witcher 3 Remaster is available September 29; the Songs of the Past DLC does not currently have a release window.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation gameplay trailer

The Weapons! Are! Here! The FFVII Revelation look out of gamescom — the first since SGF — was fairly short, focusing mostly on those giant monsters, but it did show off more of the aerial and submarine combat that’s coming in the trilogy-ending FFVII remake. Hell yeah, brother.

Final Fantasy VII Revelation comes out in spring 2027.

No Law was a fun gamescom reveal — it’s an FPS where you play as the field-tested, now peace-seeking Grey Harker. I don’t know much else about what it’s actually about, but I do know that this tongue-in-cheek, cyber-noir, gadget-driven stealth game that also lets you blow some heads off seems pretty dang fun.

No Law releases on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC in 2027.

Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu

First teaser for Aardman's stop-motion POKÉMON’ series ‘THE MISADVENTURES OF SIRFEITCH'D & PICHU’. Releasing in 2027. pic.twitter.com/6Wx7pGDb9J — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) August 28, 2026

First teaser for Aardman's stop-motion POKÉMON’ series ‘THE MISADVENTURES OF SIRFEITCH'D & PICHU’. Releasing in 2027. pic.twitter.com/6Wx7pGDb9J

Legendary animation studio Aardman (the folks behind Wallace & Gromit, Shaun the Sheep, Chicken Run, and more) revealed the first teaser for the upcoming stop-motion Sirfetch’d and Pichu teamup series at PokémonXP and holy crap, does it look super cute.

The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu releases in 2027 on Disney+.

Did we really need the return of Ali G in 2026? I dunno, probably not. Would I have preferred a Borat 3? I mean, yeah. Either way, Sacha Baron Cohen has another Ali G movie coming out this fall.

Ali G: Who Iz I? releases in theaters October 23.

POSSIBLE LOVE, a new film from Lee Chang-dong, acclaimed director of Burning and Secret Sunshine, is South Korea's Official Selection for International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards®. Two married couples cross paths to film a documentary that causes them to face their… pic.twitter.com/IKxrLsTtKW — Netflix (@netflix) August 26, 2026

POSSIBLE LOVE, a new film from Lee Chang-dong, acclaimed director of Burning and Secret Sunshine, is South Korea's Official Selection for International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards®. Two married couples cross paths to film a documentary that causes them to face their… pic.twitter.com/IKxrLsTtKW

Lee Chang-dong hasn’t made a film since 2018’s Burning. His latest, which Lee has said is 10 years in the making, has already been selected as South Korea’s Oscars entry for Best International Feature. Just from the trailer (and an excellent directorial track record; I mean, have you seen Secret Sunshine?), it’s not hard to see why Lee’s film was selected. If I feel devastated after two minutes, imagine what the power of two hours holds!

Possible Love releases in select theaters October 23 before it comes to Netflix on November 6.

This year’s Palme d’Or winner is finally crossing over to the states (and is already among extremely early whispers about Oscar nominations). The subject matter in Cristian Mungiu’s film is unpleasant: Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve’s family, with their five young children, is on the verge of being torn apart from allegations of physical abuse. Still, I’m eager to watch; Reinsve and Stan are both incredible performers.

Learn to love again. John Wilson’s THE HISTORY OF CONCRETE is in theaters starting September 18. #TheHistoryofConcrete pic.twitter.com/Qp2lDBm8d4 — Magnolia Pictures (@MagnoliaPics) August 27, 2026

Learn to love again. John Wilson’s THE HISTORY OF CONCRETE is in theaters starting September 18. #TheHistoryofConcrete pic.twitter.com/Qp2lDBm8d4

Were you a fan of the HBO show How To With John Wilson a couple years back? Were you sad when it ended? If you, like me, fall into this category, you’ll be delighted to know that Wilson has made a feature-length documentary called The History of Concrete that premiered at Sundance and is apparently very good. It finally got a trailer this week and it looks perfectly John Wilson-y.

The History of Concrete gets a limited release in theaters September 18.

First trailer for the ‘GET JIRO’ animated series. The series follows a sushi chef in a dystopian version of LA where customers resort to murder to secure a table at major restaurants. Releasing October 3 on Adult Swim. pic.twitter.com/V0Pc2LTVCK — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) August 27, 2026

First trailer for the ‘GET JIRO’ animated series. The series follows a sushi chef in a dystopian version of LA where customers resort to murder to secure a table at major restaurants. Releasing October 3 on Adult Swim. pic.twitter.com/V0Pc2LTVCK

This one’s a fun surprise: Based on the 2012 graphic novel from Joel Rose and the late Anthony Bourdain (whose biopic Tony you should see), Get Jiro is a violent animated series from DC Studios about a sushi chef who chops the head off of a customer who uses soy sauce when he explicitly said not to and grates the face off another chef (they probably also deserved it).

Get Jiro premieres on Adult Swim October 3 and streams on HBO Max the following day.

To understand the hunt, you have to understand the mind. Inspired by true events, UNABOMBER stars Russell Crowe, Jacob Tremblay, Annabelle Wallis, and Shailene Woodley. September 25. pic.twitter.com/iJTumS10Tx — Netflix (@netflix) August 27, 2026

To understand the hunt, you have to understand the mind. Inspired by true events, UNABOMBER stars Russell Crowe, Jacob Tremblay, Annabelle Wallis, and Shailene Woodley. September 25. pic.twitter.com/iJTumS10Tx

This upcoming Netflix movie — starring Jacob Tremblay as Ted Kaczynski, plus Shailene Woodley and Russell Crowe — gives off big "just-OK limited series" vibes, so I’m somewhat skeptical that this'll be any good. But I’m also dumb enough to give it a try.

Unabomber releases September 25 on Netflix.

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

articles.title: Kick Streamer Neon Responds After Rockstar Seemingly Includes a Reference to Him in GTA 6 Netflix Showcase
articles.summary: Prominent Kick streamer Neon has responded after Rockstar appeared to reference him in a side mission shown during their special GTA 6 first-look trailer on Netflix.
articles.body:
Prominent Kick streamer Neon has responded after Rockstar appeared to reference him in a side mission shown during their special GTA 6 first-look trailer on Netflix.

Rockstar broke the internet yesterday when it premiered 26 minutes of gameplay footage from Grand Theft Auto 6 on Netflix, causing brief issues on the platform and even on Twitch, where a number of streamers were reacting to the showcase in real time.

Speaking of streamers, the highly-anticipated showcase featured a side mission where Lucia steals a car — only for a content creator to hop out of the trunk after the heist is finished, asking his viewers, “Holy sh*t chat, what do I do?”

Fans couldn’t help but notice a striking resemblance between the fictional influencer and a real-life streamer named Neon. The two boast similar features and even have the same style of haircut, prompting netizens to recreate that Leonardo DiCaprio meme as they watched the preview from home.

Neon went live on Kick the next day, where he officially addressed the topic — and while he didn’t provide any solid confirmation that he truly was the inspiration for GTA 6’s streamer character, he did thank his audience for getting him popular enough to make it a legitimate theory.

"We made it! We f**kin’ did it!” an excited Neon said as he sat in the back of a car. “Shout out to everyone in the chat. I've seen some reactions: A lot of people weren't the happiest, a lot of people were showing support.

“Two streamers did text me. You know who you are, and I appreciate you. Thank you guys. …Would a B-Tier streamer really be in [this game]? Nah, I’m just kidding. That is f**kin’ sick, bro! Streaming is really taking over the game. I'm just so happy and blessed and grateful to even be seen like that, in that way.”

N3on celebrates his alleged inclusion in GTA 6 "We f'in did it..shout out to everyone in the chat..I've seen some reactions, a lot of ppl weren't the happiest, a lot of ppl were showing support..2 streamers did text me..I appreciate u..streaming is really taking over the… pic.twitter.com/FOelAyJL2q

Later that same day, Neon recreated the scene beat for beat during a live stream in a moment that went viral on social media.

NEON recreated the streamer scene from the new GTA 6 trailer perfectly 😭 pic.twitter.com/XzVLur6Cwf — ryan 🤿 (@scubaryan_) August 28, 2026

NEON recreated the streamer scene from the new GTA 6 trailer perfectly 😭 pic.twitter.com/XzVLur6Cwf

The streamer moment sparked a few big reactions from a handful of other popular broadcasters, with the likes of Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed, and Jynxi in disbelief that a content creator was included in the game.

“Wait, chat, they got streamers in the game?” a stunned IShowSpeed asked his viewers.

IShowSpeed couldn’t believe GTA 6 added streamers into the game pic.twitter.com/HDkPHoRLOH — FearBuck (@FearedBuck) August 27, 2026

IShowSpeed couldn’t believe GTA 6 added streamers into the game pic.twitter.com/HDkPHoRLOH

“Is that a streamer?” Kai Cenat shouted, his jaw dropping to the floor.

Kai Cenat finds out a streamer is on GTA 6 pic.twitter.com/sT0w3XTBvY — FearBuck (@FearedBuck) August 27, 2026

Kai Cenat finds out a streamer is on GTA 6 pic.twitter.com/sT0w3XTBvY

“They have streamers. They’re adding streamers to GTA 6,” a shocked Jynxi said. “Oh my god, it’s a brainrot IRL streamer, too!”

Jynxzi was in shock after seeing Rockstar games add IRL streamers to GTA VI 🤯 pic.twitter.com/SXpLcEHkJC — clippedbytm (@clippedbytm) August 27, 2026

Jynxzi was in shock after seeing Rockstar games add IRL streamers to GTA VI 🤯 pic.twitter.com/SXpLcEHkJC

Streamers are just one of the many real-life parallels featured in GTA 6. Check out our full coverage of the game right here on IGN, as well as a full list of all the side activities we spotted and 69 things we learned during our time at Rockstar HQ when we got a sneak peek at what’s in store come November 19.

articles.title: The 4K Restoration of a French Animation Classic Returns Us to a Trippier Era of the Art Form
articles.summary: Janus Films’ 4K restoration of René Laloux’s Gandahar returns us to a time when popping a strange-looking tape into the VHS player could yield untold delights.
articles.body:
The new 4K restoration of the uncut French version of Gandahar is being released in New York City on August 28 before expanding nationally.

Man, who remembers the crop of great, strange, watch ’em in your buddy’s finished basement (probably after a couple of bong hits) animated classics like Heavy Metal , Fantastic Planet, Wizards , and the such? Pre-internet, popping these movies into your VHS or DVD player was like playing the freak-out lottery: What weird and wonderful delights awaited you were anyone’s guess.

And now, Janus Films has unleashed a new 4K restoration of one such title, the late French animator René Laloux’s Gandahar. Laloux was also the mind behind 1973’s better-remembered cult classic Fantastic Planet (aka La Planète Sauvage). Like that film, 1987’s Gandahar is a trippy (I promise not to use that word again in this review) visit to a far-out realm, only in this case it’s a land where soulless robots attempt to overtake a seemingly utopian society, and the battle for freedom must be fought not just in the here and now, but also 1,000 years in the future. Along the way, the dangers of genetic experiments, the consequences of creating an ultimate weapon, and the effect such decisions have on future generations are all explored. Also, clothing is optional for half of these characters (the female half, as was the wont of the time).

An edited and dubbed version of the film called Light Years was released in North America by (cough) Miramax Films in 1988. That cut even featured dialogue written by legendary sci-fi scribe Isaac Asimov, who adapted the French script, but now Janus has given us the complete and original version of the sci-fi adventure. And really, the steady (sometimes somnambulistic by today’s standards) pace, the heady visuals and concepts, and the French line readings make an English version of Gandahar – voiced by the likes of John Shea, Jennifer Grey and Christopher Plummer, as Light Years apparently was – just seem wrong.

The film begins with scenes of bucolic, if strange, beauty, as a group of blue-skinned villagers fish and eat and play. An anteater-type creature is born from a plant, and immediately the babe suckles at a woman’s chest as if she’s its mother. (Maybe she is?) Birds peck at giant berries while the villagers collect them, giant snails feed while a shepherd looks on, but then suddenly… an attack! The people of Gandahar are being turned to stone by the C-3PO-like (only mean, and black) Men of Metal.

And so in the city of Jasper (which is centered in a giant statue of a woman) the leader of the Council of Women (who has huge eagle wings sticking out of the sides of her head) is advised by her lead scientist (who looks like he’s come straight out of the Green Lanterns’ Guardians of the Universe) to send out an emissary to investigate the situation. (And yes, I could keep inserting parentheticals around just about every noun in this movie to explain some kind of weirdness, which is half the film’s charm right there.)

The young “Servant” Sylvain (voiced by Pierre-Marie Escourrou) is put on the case, and while the character hits his marks as a hero – he rides a flying, flapping, funky mechanical jellyfish; shoots a gun that uses ammo which quickly propagates as spiky weeds; gets the girl; and saves the day – he’s also dry as the desert landscape where that jellyfish crash-lands. Alas, none of the human characters in this tale are particularly engaging, but that’s OK because it’s the weirdos and oddballs that Gandahar is all about.

Take the Deformed, the outcasts of Gandahar who are the result of scientific experimentation – “victims of your genetic games,” they tell Sylvain – and as such have all manner of physicality, from multiple heads to mouths for knees to my favorite, the dude who is just a huge head/chest with arms that he walks on. Also blessed/cursed with the ability to see the future, only to lose it, the Deformed now speak in the past and future tense because that’s how they see the world around them: In 1,000 years, Gandahar has fallen. 1,000 years ago, Gandahar will be saved.

Then there’s Metamorphis (Georges Wilson), a giant brain hanging out in the middle of the Eccentric Ocean, as it is rightfully called. Another forgotten legacy of Gandahar, Metamorphis is either the villain of the film or its hero, depending on your point of view. But that’s the thing about Gandahar the movie – just as its imagery is off-kilter but also beautiful, its loopy time-travel story isn’t terribly interested in adhering to traditional concepts of what an animated film needs to be. So yes, sometimes it’s slow, sometimes its hero is kind of lame, and sometimes it’s rough around the edges. But just like Fantastic Planet before it, it’s not the kind of thing that passes for big-screen animation these days, and that kind of makes it a must-watch right there. (Pass the bong.)

articles.title: Everything Coming to Amazon Prime Video in September
articles.body:
Amazon's popular Reacher series may be coming to an end in September, but plenty of other great additions are coming to the streaming service to take its place. In fact, there's a Reacher spin-off arriving on the same day of the finale to do exactly that.

If you're wondering how to make the most of your Prime Video subscription next month, I've curated a quick selection of movies and shows that are absolutely worth your time. You can also jump to the full list of September releases to see the full breakdown by day.

If you're looking for something cozy and wonderful to watch right before fall kicks off, I highly recommend Over the Garden Wall. It only ran for one season on Cartoon Network, but it has everything you could ever want in an animated series. It has some of the weirdness you'd expect from Adventure Time with just enough darkness to fit the summer-to-fall transition.

Like many other Cartoon Network favorites, it was removed from HBO Max years ago but has been available at other services since then. It also got it's first Blu-ray release this year if you'd prefer to own all 10 episodes yourself.

For fans of Jon Favreau and food, I recommend checking out 2014's Chef. It's a movie about food and family that resulted in Favreau creating a spin-off docuseries where he learns about the culinary world. Here's a quick summary of what we thought of the film in our review :

"Take away the sentiment, and the bitterness, and you’ve got a fun film about family, food, and the importance of staying true to yourself. Just make sure you eat before watching this one." - Chris Tilly

The 2004 movie starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Beckinsale is an excellent vampire hunter movie to revisit in the fall. It's a wonderful throwback to simpler times when you could just toss Wolverine into a vampire movie and it just worked. This film also came pretty shortly after Kate Beckinsale's first Underworld movie , solidifying her place in the genre forever.

The Demon Slayer series is one of the most popular anime shows in recent years. There have been four seasons and a few movies so far, so it's a great time to dive into the series for the first time.

The story is set in early 20th century Japan, centering on a teenage boy who becomes a demon hunter to avenge his family and save his sister. Amazon is also bringing the Mugen Train movie to its service, so you can catch up on most of the story pretty quickly this month.

On the same day that Reacher Season 4 comes to an end, Prime Video is dropping all eight episodes of the spin-off series at once. The show focuses on private investigator Frances Neagley as she unravels the suspicious death of her friend. Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson) will guest star in the series in a more supporting role.

IGN hasn't had the chance to watch The Love Hypothesis ahead of its release, but it's intriguing nevertheless. The movie is based on Ali Hazelwood's popular romance novel of the same name, which actually got its start as Star Wars "Reylo" fanfiction. The story is about an experiment in dating between two highly educated individuals who are trying to prove a point.

articles.title: The Founders of Hooters Are Making a Buddy-Comedy Movie About the Restaurant Chain's Origin Story
articles.summary: Yep, you read that right. Hooters: The Movie is in the early stages of pre-production, and some of the chain’s original founders are directly involved.
articles.body:
Yep, you read that right. Hooters: The Movie is in the early stages of pre-production, and some of the chain’s original founders are directly involved.

As reported by Deadline , the film is inspired by the “real events” behind Hooters’ creation, following best buds Ted and Lenny as they create a sprawling legacy for themselves with their famous ‘breastaurant’ chain — only to have their life’s work jeopardized by the US government.

Ted falls head over heels for a gal named Diane after seeing her on a TV commercial. Ted convinces Lenny to drive down with him to Clearwater Beach, Florida, where they recruit Diane to become the original Hooters Girl. The flick is described as part buddy comedy, part biopic that tells the “wild journey” of how the iconic American eatery got its start.

One of Hooters’ co-founders, Edward Droste, is both producing the film and co-authoring its screenplay. Jon Rosenbaum (Benchwarmers 2: Breaking Balls) is set to direct, and casting is already underway. Filming is scheduled to begin in November in Florida's Tampa and Clearwater areas, which is where the very first Hooters restaurant opened its doors all the way back in 1983.

“I think people are going to enjoy watching how we were really just some guys who didn’t know what we were doing, but had a great time doing it,” Droste said in a press release. “And of course, our world-famous Hooters Girls are the real stars. It’s time to deliver a taste of our big-hearted culture and famous humor to the world.”

“From the moment I first learned the Hooters origin story, I knew it would make an incredible movie,” Rosenbaum remarked. “It’s the perfect combination of a hilarious buddy comedy and an inspiring biopic for a beloved American brand: Two lifelong friends with no idea what they’re getting themselves into, a crazy idea they’re willing to bet everything on, and a wild journey that culminates in the creation of something bigger than they could ever have imagined. It’s not at all what people will be expecting – and it’s mostly true! I can’t wait to bring this story to life.”

If you’re unfamiliar, Hooters is a casual dining / sports bar chain known for its wings and its waitresses, young ladies who are often clad in white t-shirts and orange shorts. The chain was actually founded by six people: Lynn D. Stewart, Gil DiGiannantonio, Ed Droste. Billy Ranieri, Ken Wimmer, and Dennis Johnson.

At the time of writing, there are around 200 locations within the US, and 60 internationally in areas including the Bahamas, the Czech Republic, Japan, Switzerland, and more.

articles.title: Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Will Send You On a Chilly Loot Grind | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: Dragon's Dogma 2's Dark Arisen expansion adds a whole new region with clever winter weather effects, an old-but-new loot grind, and... a dragon that vomits zombies. We're so back.
articles.body:
There are plenty of fantastical creatures to fight in Dragon’s Dogma 2, but nowhere in the base game will you find a dragon that vomits zombies. You will find such a beast in its upcoming Dark Arisen expansion, though, and this winged atrocity marked the final challenge of a 90-minute hands-on demo I played just ahead of gamescom 2026.

The undead barfer easily ranks among Dragon’s Dogma 2’s most hideous foes – a scaly titan with an unsightly face, torn wings, and decaying flesh. At multiple points throughout the battle, it rears back its head to belch a plume of sinister smoke from its rotting maw, out of which skitters a gang of pallid corpses. It’s a creative and horrific way to introduce additional mobs to a boss fight, and for a moment I’m distracted from my project of hacking the dragon’s legs off to perform a series of spinning sword attacks, cutting down the newly-birthed fodder three at a time.

Such a beast awaits you in Norgan, the new “Forsaken Dominion” that Dark Arisen adds to the north of the base game’s map. While designed for advanced players, it’s not an “end game” zone; instead, it’s recommended for characters around level 40, and can be accessed from relatively early in the campaign. The region’s icy conditions and bitter snowstorms create several new and unique challenges, and outfitting yourself to survive such sub-zero temperatures is first on the agenda. The demo opens with a blacksmith offering to craft me some armour with better thermal properties, and a short fetch quest later I’m outfitted in furs fit for a Stark. While the demo didn’t allow me the chance to fully explore why warmer armour is so important – does the cold inflict damage over time, like in the modern Zelda games? Or does thermal clothing provide better defense against icy attacks? – my short trek into the frigid north still highlighted a number of ways the region’s climate poses dangers distinct from those we’ve faced in more southern lands.

While battling against the yeti-like Norgan giant, I was frozen solid by the beast’s arctic breath. Later, midway through the fight, an unexpected avalanche knocked me off my feet, disrupting my chain of attacks. As ever, your AI companion Pawns chatter away, and their dialogue hints to such avalanches being triggered by both large beasts and your own weapon strikes. Other tactics suggested by my party include rolling a boulder towards an enemy, which would grow larger as it gathered up the snow in its path, and shattering hanging icicles so they would rain down like glass on our foes.

“I definitely didn't want the cold, snowy region to purely be a visual effect,” Dark Arisen’s director, Kenta Kinoshita, tells me. “If a snowstorm has blown in and is obscuring your visibility and the wind is working against you, then you're going to have to come up with a way to get around it. But the wind can also be used to your advantage; if you're trying to jump over a gap in a crevice and you're able to orient yourself towards the direction the wind's blowing, it can blow you further. The wind could even be a help in getting you on top of huge enemies if you orient yourself right.”

The base game encouraged you to use the world around you as a tool and a weapon, a philosophy Dark Arisen is expanding upon further. Kinoshita describes how enemies will cross frozen lakes in pursuit of you, and so you can break the ice to plunge them into the water below (it’s here where it's worth remembering that Dragon’s Dogma 2’s water is plagued by The Brine, the red tentacled mass which swallows up any living thing.)

“There could be an enemy that steals your relics and runs away,” Kinoshita adds. “How do you find where it's gone? Well, follow the footprints in the snow and maybe you'll trace it back to its nest and find the relics that it's stolen from you and more besides. At every different level of encounter design, I wanted the cold theme to [provide] a level of friction that's really interesting for the player to discover and then strategize on how to overcome.”

By relics, Kinoshita doesn’t just mean any old piece of equipment you’ve found. Relics are part of Dark Arisen’s new loot system that sees you collect mystery spoils from across Norgan and bring them back to camp to be “appraised” by Jiera, the local wise woman. When acquired, relics are listed in your inventory with vague descriptions – this one is a helm, this is a light weapon – and are utterly useless to you. Throw Jiera a few rift crystals, though, and she’ll reveal their true nature, turning them into gear you can carry into battle. Compared to the equipment discovered in the base game, relics are more likely to have interesting properties that you could build a strategy around, such as substantial stat modifiers or abilities.

One of the demo’s early quests paired me up with Freki, a huge direwolf with a taste for hare and a nose for relics. Following your first scripted adventure, you can feed Freki meat whenever you want to trigger his hunt for buried relics – simply follow him to acquire new treasures.

This new system intrigues me because it encourages a very particular gameplay loop, one reminiscent of the loot grinds in games like Destiny. Many Diablo-esque ARPGs and looter shooters use randomised rewards that must be “decoded” as a way of establishing a compelling cycle of explore, collect, decipher, equip, repeat. The bait, of course, is the possibility of finding that one piece of gear that will elevate your character build and unlock the ability to complete the cycle in even more dangerous parts of the world, which in turn rewards even greater weapons and armour.

Kinoshita agrees that this more organic style of play is a focus for Dark Arisen, beyond the traditional framework of a fantasy RPG. “There are, of course, quests. You'll unlock them and follow along the storyline,” he explains, “but as they relate to the relic system, they're more of a means to give the player a reason to go out and explore different areas.”

If the relic system sounds familiar but you’re not well acquainted with Destiny’s Master Rahool, then it may be because you’re a long-term Dragon’s Dogma fan who remembers the original’s expanded re-release, also called Dark Arisen. Scattered across that game’s Bitterblack Isle dungeon was cursed loot, items that needed to be purified before use. The similarity between the cursed loot and relic systems, as well as the fact that both expansions are called Dark Arisen, is no coincidence.

“We wanted to add a similar relic exploration and appraisal cycle to Dragon’s Dogma 2,” confirms producer Naoto Oyama, “but this time we thought it was better to focus on a new wide area to build upon the open game design that everyone loves so much.” And so, rather than just a single dungeon, this new version of Dark Arisen’s loot system takes place across an entire region.

It’s interesting that Capcom has elected to free the loot cycle from the confines of a single dungeon, but still keep it contained within the borders of one biome. The studio could have introduced relics into the wider world, allowing them to be discovered in the lands of Vermund and Battahl – that would certainly encourage veteran players to return to lands they’ve already rinsed clean. But Capcom’s decision is backed up by a clear purpose.

“In order to keep the new area distinct, [Norgan] is the only place in which the actual relic acquisition and appraisal cycle takes place,” Kinoshita explains. “But you're not locked into Norgan once you travel there. You can travel back to the original map and use that acquired gear to take on further challenges, especially the 12 new Lost Rites dungeons.”

These new dungeons represent some of Dark Arisen’s greatest challenges. In their depths lie rare, incredibly desirable equipment. I didn’t get to set foot in any of them as part of this demo, but the allure is strong.

“They ramp up in challenge as they go along,” says Kinoshita. “You can choose how much you want to do [Dark Arisen’s] two different contents in parallel. For instance, you might explore some of the earlier Lost Rites dungeons and then get to quite a challenging one you're not quite ready for. You could then go to Norgan and start to find relics as a way to prepare yourself to finish the next dungeon. And so there's an interaction between those two different areas and elements, even though the actual relic drops and appraisal only happen specifically in Norgan.”

When I first realised what Dark Arisen was doing with loot, I’ll admit to feeling somewhat disappointed – I play RPGs for questing and story, and any kind of grind cycle with randomised loot is typically something that repels me. But I think it makes sense for Dragon’s Dogma 2, which thrives when you leave the well-trodden path behind and trek through the wilderness in search of your own story. While I hope the main questline features more complex design than the fetch tasks this demo offered, all my best memories of the base game were organic discoveries. The relic system appears to encourage even more of that, and the challenge posed by the Lost Rites dungeons will hopefully push us into delving deep into the far reaches of this expansion’s new land.

I doubt Dark Arisen will turn non-believers into Dragon’s Dogma 2 converts, but for those who already love its unique approach to the open-world RPG, this expansion promises to bolster the idiosyncrasies you know and love with ideas old and new.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Join Us: Watch 11 Minutes of Exclusive Gameplay from the Upcoming Cult Simulator | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: Wolf Haus Games revealed 11 minutes of gameplay for Join Us at gamescom 2026, alongside a PS5 announcement and a trailer featuring real-life former cult members.
articles.body:
Join Us, the upcoming open-world co-op game where you can start your very own doomsday cult, just dropped a ton of new gameplay as part of IGN's gamescom programming. You can see more than 11 minutes of exclusive footage in the player below, and get a deeper look into just how the game will work.

Earlier this week, developer Wolf Haus games announced that the darkly satirical survival/action cult simulator will be available on PS5 at launch alongside the PC and Xbox Series X/S versions in March 2027. The news of Join Us' PS5 version also featured information on how 4-player co-op will work in both the campaign and free roam.

In addition to the extended gameplay, IGN can exclusively reveal a special video from Wolf Haus showing four real-life former cult members coming together to play Join Us in co-op and reflicting on their past histories while enjoying this new adventure and reacting to the game

The live-action trailer featuring former cult members, which you can watch below, introduces us to Jaga, Javier, Ariel, and Elena - who have a "collective experience of over 50 years in their unique societies." This experience involves a cult that is preparing for aliens to arrive on Earth and take us back to the planet we came from, a peaceful cult that focuses on martial arts and self-defense training, and a holistic rejuvenation cult.

In Join Us, players will need to stay vigilant though, as they'll need to keep their recruits happy or they will leave the cult. As the devs put it, "a cult leader without any followers is just a lonely weirdo."

For more from gamescom, be sure to check out everything that was revealed during Opening Night Live.

articles.title: Philips OneBlade vs Standard Razors: A Worthwhile Upgrade?
articles.summary: The Philips OneBlade is available at a discount right now at Amazon - here's why it's ideal for your next shave.
articles.body:
If there’s one part of consumer technology that’s seen pretty understated leaps in the last few decades, it’s personal grooming.

Whether it’s trimming your beard and trying not to remove a layer of your skin in doing so, or somewhere even more personal, the time of the manual razor is over. Here’s why you need to ditch it, and why the Philips OneBlade is a great alternative .

Save Your Shave With This OneBlade 360 Discount

While a good, old-fashioned razor might seem like an obvious way to trim away your five-o’clock shadow or touch up your facial hair, it’s not exactly something I’ve ever looked forward to.

In fact, growing up, I used to dread having to shave because the razors back in my day (yes, I’m going full Grandpa Simpson) would leave me cut up and peppered with bits of tissue to stem the bleeding.

Even shaving creams, foams, and lotions did little to make the experience feel anything other than torturous, and that’s just the face - drift to your pits, or–heaven forbid–below the belt, and you’ll be feeling itchy, sore, or worse for days.

So what of the OneBlade? For one thing, as the name suggests, it’s delightfully simple. You can use it on your boat race, you can use it on your body, and yes, you can use it on your more delicate areas, too.

While you can use shaving foam or cream with it, I find it to be just as comfortable without it, and while new heads are hardly cheap, at least that’s another expense you can get by without.

The newer OneBlade 360 version actually follows the contours of your face, too, letting you more easily mop up any bits you may have missed. OneBlade is also waterproof, making it ideal for use in the shower (don’t forget to unclog your drain, you animals), and the blades are easy to clean. Each blade lasts around four months, too, and once it does get blunt, you can swiftly swap it over with a quick release mechanism.

Battery life is great, and while I'd have liked a USB-C charging port, as long as you remember where you put the charging cable then you're all set - plus replacements are cheap to pick up if you do lose it (speaking from experience).

Better yet, it’s discounted by 27% at the time of writing. That means you can get the OneBlade 360, with an additional blade, three stubble combs, a storage pouch and a charging cable for just £32.97. The whole set would usually cost £44.99, so you’re getting everything you need at a great price.

Trust me when I say I wish I had this when I was younger - don’t make the same mistake I did! Your face (and everywhere else) will thank you for it.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Everything Coming to Netflix in September
articles.summary: Welcome in the fall with the xenomorph, some T-virus zombies, Bruce the shark, and more... all on Netflix
articles.body:
Netflix is wrapping up the summer with the Jaws movies, the Resident Evil flicks, and both Alien and Aliens while also getting into the back-to-school spirit with a revival of '80s/'90s Cosby Show spin-off, A Different World.

You can also catch some great spookies with Ready or Not, Smile 2, Oculus, and the Texas Chainsaw Massacre reboot from 2003. Plus, there's solid gold cinema like Phantom Thread, About Time, Knocked Up, Liar Liar, Dragnet, and Cruel Intentions! There's also new sophomore seasons of Guy Ritchie's The Gentlemen (which was already picked up for a third season) and Stranger Things: Tales From '85.

So while you ponder the how/why/who of Netflix raising its prices once again , here's a rundown of every series, special, movie, and doc landing on Netflix in September...

If you're just looking for a detailed list of everything coming to Netflix this month, you can jump to the full release schedule by day.

2022's Smile was a serviceable slice of spooky for sure, but Smile 2 is a horror masterclass in crafting a much much better sequel, thanks in no small part to Naomi Scott's superb performance as a spread-too-thin pop star trying to make a comeback after a personal tragedy. Writer/director Parker Finn takes the fiendishly fun idea from his first flick and blows it up in bold, beautiful ways.

Good Place alums Andrew Law, Matt Murray, and Mike Schur present us with Dang!, an adult animated comedy starring Law, Stephanie Hsu (Everything Everywhere All at Once), and Poppy Liu (Hacks) about a brother and sister whose fun lives in New York City get ruined when their high-achieving older sister shows up and wants to hang out.

All three seasons of the blistering catering biz comedy, Party Down, is headed to Netflix. Razor sharp and starring the likes of Adam Scott, Jane Lynch, Ken Marino, Lizzy Caplan, and more, Party Down also boasts Paul Rudd and Rob Thomas (iZombie, Veronica Mars) among its co-creators/writers. We should note, though, that the third season is a six-episode revival from 2023, featuring most of the cast as everything that once held cult comedy currency returns to us in some way or another... unless it's the Community movie, which seems like it'll never happen.

This revival of the famed Cosby Show spin-off, A Different World, takes us back to Hillman College and follows Deborah (Maleah Joi Moon), the youngest child of Kadeem Hardison's Dwayne Wayne and Jasmine Guy's Whitley Gilbert as she finds her parents' shadow difficult to escape during her first year. Along with the new cast, show (and Hillman) alumni Hardison, Guy, Darryl M. Bell, Cree Summer, Charnele Brown, Ajai Sanders, Dawnn Lewis, and Jada Pinkett Smith are back as well.

Any time we hear that writer/director Mike Flanagan and his Flana-gang are tackling a new Stephen King adaptation (like Flanagan's upcoming Carrie miniseries ), we get super pumped. But let's also give it up for Flanagan originals, like your Midnight Mass. your Hush, and...your Oculus — a savage, scary look at a family ripped apart by a cursed object. Starring Karen Gillan, Katee Sackhoff, and Kate Siegel (duh!), Oculus is cinematic dread in all the best ways.

Starring Jacob Tremblay, Russell Crowe, Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis, and Alexander Ludwig, Unabomber alternates between two timelines to track the story of domestic terrorist Ted Kaczynski from his time at Harvard to the nationwide manhunt decades later. Janus Metz Pedersen (Andor) directs.

articles.title: IGN's Top-Reviewed Nintendo Switch 2 Games
articles.summary: Not all Nintendo games are created equal. Here are the 10 best Nintendo games we've played in the Switch 2 generation.
articles.body:
The Switch 2 launched just over a year ago, and we've already gotten our hands on some excellent games . If you're looking for recommendations of what to play on the newest console, we've compiled every Nintendo game that we've given a review score of 8 or above.

While there are tons of amazing games that have already been released on or ported over to the Switch 2, we’re setting some limits by sticking to Nintendo exclusives. These are predominantly first-party games published by Nintendo for either just the Switch 2 or both Switch consoles.

From IGN's Review: " The leader of the bunch is finally back to kick some tail in Donkey Kong Bananza, a brilliant successor to Super Mario Odyssey and a smashing return for a classic Nintendo character. It was a bold choice to build the Switch 2’s first 3D platformer around Donkey Kong instead of Mario, but it’s proven to be the best decision Nintendo could’ve made. DK’s satisfying, expressive movement and powerful, dynamic abilities create a truly groundbreaking adventure." - Logan Plant

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom - Switch 2 Edition

From IGN's Review Update: "Not only does The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom still hold up as a game I can’t wait to lose a few dozen more hours in, the updates and additions made to the Switch 2 Edition make it feel like this is the way it was always meant to be played." - Tom Marks

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild - Switch 2 Edition

From IGN's Review Update: "This Nintendo Switch 2 Edition is of course an enhanced version with visual upgrades, faster loading times, and support for the Zelda Notes service via the Nintendo Switch App on your mobile device. It’s admittedly a fairly modest upgrade in terms of actual new features or content, but a welcome one, and it makes this undoubtedly the best way to play a sprawling epic that still stands tall as one of the greatest achievements in Nintendo’s iconic adventure series." - Tristan Ogilvie

From IGN's Review: "Splatoon Raiders is an amazing action RPG with an expertly executed loop. It has fantastic new powers with crazy upgrades that are worth chasing, tough battles that force you to put care into your build in order to overcome them, and a huge variety of fun level types to jump between. The pacing, balance, and difficulty curve are very impressive: I always had to work to get better, but none of the campaign ever felt like grinding or needless padding." - Logan Plant

From IGN's Review: "Pokémon Pokopia is a real treat: an enjoyable building and town simulator that capitalizes on the charming personalities of its monsters in a way that appeals to both the creative and collector alike. It's packed with fun things to do and worthy rewards for doing them, and strikes a healthy balance between freedom and suggestion in its building mechanics (despite a few precision nitpicks)." - Rebekah Valentine

From IGN's Review: "The first brand-new Mario Kart in a decade makes huge changes to the established formula, but ironically, the best parts about it closely follow the blueprint of every entry that’s come before: unbeatable local multiplayer racing on well-designed tracks that more than live up to the series’ legacy. World’s tight controls, celebratory soundtrack, and universal polish marvelously complement the action, and I can’t wait to see how top players will take full advantage of its exciting parkour mechanics in the months and years ahead." - Logan Plant

From IGN's Review: "Despite knowing nearly all Star Fox 64’s shortcuts and secrets for close to 30 years now, this remake’s impressive coat of paint and compelling new cutscenes made me smile like I just did my very first barrel roll. Finding hidden routes to unlock different stages or small optimizations to push my score sky high is still much deeper than it first appears, keeping the brief campaign runs fun across multiple playthroughs." - Jada Griffin

From IGN's Review: "I’m not sure what’s crazier: the fact that Kirby Air Riders exists, or the fact that it’s this great. It’s a blast in local or online multiplayer during its traditional races and unique battle mode, and its frankly absurd amount of fun achievements to chase, meaningful unlockables, and deep customization makes it great for solo players, too." - Logan Plant

From IGN's Review: "It nails the essential elements of a Prime game that remain special decades later: tense exploration through haunting locations highlighted by amazing worldbuilding, breathtaking art direction, new twists on classic abilities, and flawless technical performance. Even though a few underdeveloped elements keep it from feeling as cohesive as its predecessors, Prime 4 reaches heights worthy of the Metroid name." - Logan Plant

Super Mario Bros. Wonder + Meetup in Bellabel Park - Switch 2 Edition

From IGN's Review: "It sands off the rough edges of the original version while adding a fantastic lineup of boss battles, endgame challenges, and cooperative levels that each make use of Wonder’s excellent platforming in entirely different ways. The local and online competitive minigames are pretty bland, and I wish it’d gone just a bit further in getting the most out of its exciting new Dual Badge idea, but the rest of this expansion is so polished and inspired that it more than makes up for any shortcomings." - Logan Plant

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: We Played State of Decay 3 and It's In Good Shape Despite the Xbox Upheaval
articles.summary: State of Decay 3 seems to be showing promise after playing an action-packed 30 minutes of an early alpha build.
articles.body:
It's been a tumultuous time for development teams around the Xbox umbrella, including Undead Labs which is in the process of changing ownership amid the "Xbox reset." This left us with tons of questions about the state of its upcoming zombie-survival game State of Decay 3 and if it'd even see the light of day. Well, I played it at gamescom 2026 and I'm happy to report that the short 30-minute demo I saw and went hands-on with shows a lot of promise. Even as an early alpha build, I got a good impression of the improved gunplay and movement, and the general feeling that this is a State of the Decay worthy of the current generation while building on the series' fundamentals.

This is still very much about community management and base-building, both of which have been expanded in a few notable ways. From what I saw, facilities and buildings don't necessarily have linear upgrade paths and can instead specialize in specific functions through branching upgrades. What's just as important is which characters you assign to which facilities – for example, those who have perks or traits suited for the medical field can boost the rate at which other survivors will recover.

What I saw in greater detail was the deeper trait system where every procedurally assembled character has their own set of perks and quirks that can evolve. These kinds of systems were a core part of State of Decay 2, and they seem to have a greater impact now. One survivor had the trait of "takes long showers," thus taking up more water resources to maintain the settlement. But he was also adept at melee combat, so perhaps his showering habits are worth the trade-off for when you want to use him in the field. Another character had a trait that said she had sniper training, offering extra damage with long-range guns and for headshots, but she was more injury prone – and with a more granular injury system that calculates damage to specific body parts and applies debuffs to certain functions (like weapon accuracy or movement speed as examples), it's something you have to take into consideration more than previous games.

When you're managing 30-plus characters, accounting for these traits can make for a really interesting dynamic when deciding who to control when fighting zombies in the field and who you assign back at base. My hope is that they'll be as impactful in the long-run as they were in the immediate hands-on I got.

But State of Decay has always been just as much about fending off hordes of zombies, and things work differently in State of Decay 3. There are plenty of towns, facilities, and general points of interest that make up its large open world and when you pull up the map, you'll see infestation networks spreading all across the world and branching into adjacent towns. Infested settlements and plague nests are the hotspots you want to hit in order to cut off the spread, and these make for intense battles.

There is always a heart of the infestation at these locations, sometimes buried beneath a facility or in the garage of an autoshop, and some could be more intricate dungeon-style areas. But it seems regardless of location, you need to find four of its weak points spread across the location in order to destroy it. You're also fending off a bunch of zombies in the process, and once you've opened the heart of the infestation, an even bigger zombie horde will come after you. It's absolute chaos when you're pumping all of your remaining bullets into the heart as bloaters and juggernauts back up the zombie wave, but once it's destroyed, the remaining zombies die out.

It sounds simple enough, but for me, the smoother and punchier gunplay helps the moment-to-moment combat feel a lot better than previous entries. It was evident with the AK-47 with a drum mag that I used to slay zombie crowds and the silenced pistol for one-tap headshots, and that was scratching the surface – I also saw how you can lure and bait groups into flammable oil spills, or use stealth more effectively to shave off a few zombies before all hell breaks loose. There's a running slide you can do to knock weaker zombies down and execute a finisher to keep the standard melee bat-swining more interesting. And as mentioned earlier, these playstyles can be further emphasized when controlling survivors with skills and traits suited for them. Overall, State of Decay 3 plays like a proper third-person shooter, and it's a great contrast to the management sim we come to the series for.

At least from this early version, it seems that the main thrust of State of Decay 3 is map-wide territory control by way of clearing out infestation sites and keeping them from coming back. Over time, infestations will spring back up and sieges on established settlements will also pose a persistent threat, which is the juggling act of survival games and something the series is familiar with. So, in the process of gathering food, water, and other utilities to keep your survivors going, there's that simulation running in the background to keep you on your toes.

Of course, there's drop-in / drop-out co-op multiplayer in State of Decay 3 and without limitations on how players within the session explore the open world. The team at Undead Labs also referenced a sort of dynamic difficulty system that makes sure that you're not blasting through zombies with total ease; it may lay off the gas pedal if you're repeatedly running into a wall as well. These are all things that are sure to be worked out as development continues, as well as the somewhat rough technical performance of the early alpha build I played.

More broadly, I hope that this dynamic of territory control via combat and settlement management sim can hold my interest when it comes time to put hours and hours into it as I did with State of Decay 2. It took time for Undead Labs to get its previous game in a good spot and is now a pretty robust package, and perhaps this upcoming entry can come out of the gate stronger.

The team is sticking to having a closed playtest toward the end of 2026 with a full release sometime in 2027 for Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, and PC via Steam. We have plenty of hands-on previews from gamescom 2026, so be sure to check out our first impressions of Fable's combat , Gears of War: E-Day's campaign , and Metro 2039 .

He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. articles.title: The Fibbage Card Game Brings the Best Jackbox Party Game to the Tabletop and It's Just as Great as You Remember
articles.body:
If you were attending parties in the mid 2010s, there is a pretty good chance that at least some of those gatherings you partook in the party game “Fibbage” from the folks behind Jackbox Games . This digital party game has gone on to spawn multiple iterations over the 12 years since the first was released back in 2014, and now Jackbox Games is cutting the cable and bringing this mainstay party game to the tabletop with a card-based version for your board game nights.

All of the rules that have helped make this digital bluffing game have carried over to this new card game. As in the other iterations, in Fibbage one of the players will serve as a “revealer” who will draw a card and read aloud a prompt with a portion blanked out, and it is up to the other players to write down a plausible option to complete the prompt. However, the person who drew the prompt will have the correct answer and will write it down and add it as the correct answer. The players will all put in their answers, which will be shuffled, followed by a voting period where you vote for which you think is the right answer. From there, points are earned based on whether you guessed right and if others voted for your submission, and the person with the most points at the end of however many rounds you decide on (by default it’s six rounds) wins.

Inside the box, which is roughly the size of a standard hardcover book, the rules are on a single side of paper (the other side is an ad for Jackbox Party Pack 4 ), cardboard voting/point tokens (but strangely no bag to put them in), six dry-erase markers with boards, and 300 cards with prompts. The prompts themselves span an eclectic range of topics, from asking about chefs who cook ducks with hair dryers to Japan-exclusive flavors of Pepsi. The impressive number of cards means you will have a good number of games to get through before you start getting many repeats, which is great.

The Fibbage Card Game, just like the digital version , is ripe for expansion after expansion, and knowing Jackbox, I imagine it won’t be long until we start seeing packs of additional prompt cards, different themed prompts, and extra markers and boards to write on. There really isn’t any reason that you can’t expand the player count to as high as you want, so long as you have things to write with and on, and something to keep track of the points with.

Everything about Fibbage has made the jump to a physical game rather successfully, with one slight exception - the writing the answer part. Does it work? Sure. The issue is that considering the revealer knows that answer, unless your group has really similar handwriting, or at least writing box letters similarly (which the game suggests you use), before too long you will probably start recognizing the handwriting of the players. Especially in lower player count games. A situation I ran into.

A bit of homebrew magic I worked out was that I had the revealer gather the submissions, then, on a separate sheet of paper, copy down all the answers, and the group would vote on that list. It does add an extra step and a little more time, but this does manage to keep the votes tied to the answer as opposed to everyone pretending they are a forensic document examiner (I looked that one up; an FDE looks at and compares handwriting and signatures for the court - also may or may not be a question on one of the cards).

Regardless of how you play it, Fibbage ranks up there as one of my favorite purely party games out there . It's one of those games that even ol’ grandma and grandpa can get in on and have a good time with. I’ve always appreciated the fact that Fibbage asks a bit more of its players, requiring you to be a bit more clever and creative without relying so much on “who has the funniest response” to score points. An outcome that I’ve found games of Cards Against Humanity and others tend to devolve into. This physical version of Fibbage is a really faithful adaptation of a game with a proven track record of being a hit at parties, and one I can see myself bringing out frequently.
